extracted.intended_audience: members of Parliament, Board of Control, and East India Company officials (and readers of the appended correspondence)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts of official representations and letters (1782–1784) concerning the Nabob of Arcot, Company finances, alleged misconduct by a Governor, and directions from the Commissioners; includes policy directives, complaints, and procedural points about debt settlement and conduct of servants. Intended as documentary material for parliamentary/Company decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Company servants engaging in loans with country powers
rubrics_metrics.description: “no person, being a servant of the Company, or being under our protection, shall, on any pretence whatever, be concerned in any loan or other money transaction with any of the country powers, unless with the knowledge and express permission of our respective governments.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any servant or person under Company protection discovered counteracting these orders should be sent home to England to be punished as guilty of disobedience of orders; no protection or assistance of the Company shall be given for the recovery of any loans connected with such transactions; particular attention enjoined and connivance will incur highest displeasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on intercourse between British subjects and the Nabob and his family
rubrics_metrics.description: “we repeat our prohibition in the strongest terms respecting any intercourse between British subjects and the Nabob and his family; as we are convinced that such an intercourse has been carried on greatly to the detriment and expense of the Nabob, and merely to the advantage of individuals.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All persons who shall offend against the letter and spirit of this order, whether in the Company's service or under their protection, be forthwith sent to England.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company's claim to arrears takes priority over private creditors
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our right to be paid the arrears of those expenses by which, almost to our own ruin, we have preserved the country and all the property connected with it from falling a prey to a foreign conqueror, surely stands paramount to all claims for former debts upon the revenues of a country so preserved...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court of Directors asserts it cannot consent to give up any part of the seven lacs (agreed arrears) to private creditors until the Company's debt is discharged; strong dissent to appropriation of the fund to private creditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve opportunity to question justice and origin of private debts
rubrics_metrics.description: “the opportunity of questioning, within the limited time, the justice of any of the debts, ought to have been fully preserved... how far the express direction of the act to examine the nature and origin of the debts has been by the amended paragraphs complied with...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court submits that examination should include rate of interest (e.g., soucar assignments acting as native bankers) and reasonableness of deductions (such as the 25% directed by Bengal government) — i.e., not merely mechanical approval but inquiry into nature, origin, and accumulation of debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debts to be computed with simple interest only (not compound)
rubrics_metrics.description: “This it was not our intention to allow; and lest any misconception should arise on the spot, we have added an express direction that the debts be made up with simple interest only, from the time of their respective consolidation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit direction (Clause F f) that compound interest is not to be allowed in making up private debts — guidance for how debt totals are to be calculated for settlement purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: If revenue deficiency arises, payments apportioned proportionally
rubrics_metrics.description: “if, notwithstanding the provisions contained in our former paragraphs, any deficiency should arise, the payments of what shall be received shall be made in the same proportion which would have obtained in the division of the whole twelve lacs, had they been paid.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid placing any deficiency wholly on a single class of debts; preserve proportional division across classes as originally apportioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious accusations of corruption require inquiry and protection of honest governors
rubrics_metrics.description: “as the letters... contain matter and... charge the most enormous crimes... common decency and common policy demanded an inquiry into their truth or falsehood.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessity to inquire into such charges: protect the honest fame of virtuous governors and punish the corrupt and tyrannical; if accusations are forgeries, censure falls on the accuser; consider measures to secure government against infamous accusations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government records and accounts must not be fabricated or erased
rubrics_metrics.description: Passage noting that a Governor “has the fabrication of the records in his own hands” and had “ordered the sums to be struck off, and the accounts to be erased from the cash-book of the Company.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied standard that records and accounts should be accurate, not falsified or erased; such manipulation undermines ability to investigate and justify conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrators must secure grain supplies and avoid policies that cause famine
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints that rice purchased for the Nabob was seized by Lord Macartney with a military force and that prohibitory orders to private merchants and forbidding private grain sales have contributed to famine and suffering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied policy criterion: governors should allow and encourage private merchants to supply grain and draw on northern supplies; avoid seizure/prohibitions that prevent private importation and thereby cause famine; ensure provisions for army and population.
